en: The Sūtra of the Twenty-One Homages to the Noble Tārā, translated by Anzang,
Academician and Chief Counselor of the Hanlin Academy,
Grand Master of the Second Class, by Imperial Decree.
Oṃ! Homage to Tārā, the swift and heroic; Tāre, you who dispel all fears!
Ture, you who bestow the supreme meaning! I praise and pay homage to you, O Lady endowed with the syllable Svāhā.
Homage to the Savior, the Swift Heroine, Whose eyes shine like flashes of lightning.
Homage to the Mother whose lotus-face is the Honored One of the three worlds, appearing with exquisite beauty from within a wondrous flower;
who possesses a face that is universally perfect and stainless,
like a thousand stars gathered at once, her sublime majesty surpassing them all.
Homage to the Mother of purple-golden hue, Whose hands are beautifully adorned with exquisite lotuses;
To her who bestows diligent practice, gentleness, and tranquility, And whose nature is defined by patience and meditative concentration—
Homage to the Mother of the Tathāgata’s Uṣṇīṣa, The most supreme, capable of fulfilling boundless conduct.
Having reached the further shore without remainder, you are most dearly beloved by the sons of the Victorious One;
I pay homage to you, Tāra HŪṂ, the Mother of Syllables.
With the sound of your voice filling the quarters and the expanse of space, you traverse and tread upon the seven worlds with your feet, able to summon and gather all beings without exception.
Homage to the Mother of Śakra, Brahmā, and Agni;
To the hosts of Vāyu, the Īśvaras, the gathered Bhūtas, Vetālas, and Gandharvas;
To the assembly of Yakṣas who offer praise—homage to the Mother Tretīyā, Who utterly destroys the ritual applications of others.
Extending the left and curling the right, she plants her foot;
Her topknot blazes with extreme brilliance—homage to the Great Tārā!
Valiantly able to crush the hosts of māras and enemies, With a lotus face knit in a frown, she destroys all multitudes of adversaries.
Homage to the Mother of the Seal of the Three Jewels’ Array, whose fingers are held at her heart in a majestic and adorned form,
who pervades the entire mandala of the directions without exception;
homage to the Mother of Splendor and Joy, a mass of blazing light from her own body, adorned with a jeweled crown and garlands of pearls.
Homage to the Mother who guards all stages, who laughs most fiercely with *ḍāṭṭahāsa*,
who subdues the worldly māras, and who inspires reverence;
she who can summon the hosts of deities with a frowning brow and the syllable *hūṃ*, and who brings liberation from all decline.
Homage to the Mother whose crown bears the form of the moon, In whose diadem appears the sublime and wondrous radiance of Amitābha Buddha,
Whose topknot constantly emits the light of myriad exquisite jewels;
Homage to the Mother who resembles the end of the kalpa-fire, Who dwells within her blazing, radiant topknot.
Universally joyful, seated in the half-lotus posture, Able to destroy the wheel of evil enemies—
homage to the Mother who presses the earth with her hand! Trampling with her feet to suppress,
she manifests a frowning face and utters the sound "HŪṂ," Able to shatter the seven perils and subjugate all that is to be tamed.
Homage to the Mother who is peaceful, gentle, and kind, The realm of supreme bliss, the nirvāṇa of cessation, svāhā!
Through the union with the seed-syllable of life, She is well able to extinguish great calamities.
Homage to the Mother of Universal Great Joy, Who causes all enemies to be severed from their limbs.
Adorned with the exquisite arrangement of the ten-syllable mantra, The vidyā-mantra constantly radiant with the sound of HŪṂ;
Homage to the Mother Duritapati! With her feet poised in the *mīlumantha* posture, she shakes The three realms at these three locations.
*Mīlumanthakrīḍasva* (Play the *mīlumantha* dance! *Hūṃ* (the seed syllable) *Phaṭ* (the seal) *Trilokam ākampaya* (Shake the three worlds!)
Homage to the Mother, the Ocean of *Sarasvatī*, who holds the image of the divine beast in her hand and utters the sound of the two *tāra*s; she who can extinguish all poisons without exception.
Homage to the Mother, the assembly of all deities, the beloved refuge of the gods and *kiṃnaras*.
Majestic, joyful, and firm as armor, she who extinguishes strife and evil dreams;
homage to the Mother of the Broad and Full Moon and Sun, whose gaze surpasses universal illumination.
By reciting the two *hara-dut-tarī* mantras, she skillfully removes malignant poisons and fevers.
Homage to the Mother endowed with the three truths, Who possesses the power of perfect tranquility;
To the yakṣī Vetālī, who utterly dispels calamities—
If there is a wise person who applies themselves with diligence, They should recite these twenty-one names with a sincere heart.
I pay sincere homage to the Honored One who delivers [beings]; therefore, I praise the root mantra.
Every morning upon rising and every evening at dusk, I pay homage;
by recollecting this, I bestow supreme fearlessness upon all, and all karmic offenses are completely eliminated, enabling one to transcend all evil realms.
These will swiftly enable one to attain wisdom;
through the empowerment of seven hundred million Buddhas, one shall enjoy worldly wealth and long life in this present age.

Even when approaching the state of all Buddhas in the future, should one at some time mistakenly consume various poisons—whether naturally occurring or synthetically compounded—[they shall be neutralized].
Recalling the true power of the Noble One, all evil poisons are utterly destroyed.
Whether one sees another afflicted by malevolent spirits or suffering from fever and various ailments,
if this praise is recited two, three, or seven times, all those sufferings and afflictions will be entirely dispelled.
If you pray for sons or daughters, you shall obtain sons or daughters; if you seek wealth, treasures, or rank, you shall obtain abundance and prosperity.
This root ten-syllable mantra, which is perfectly capable of fulfilling all wishes according to one's intent, cannot be assailed by any obstacles:

*Oṃ Tāre Tuttāre Ture Svāhā*. The Mantra for Deliverance from the Eight Difficulties: *Oṃ Tāre Tuttāre Ture Sarvabhayaparitrāṇi Sarvadurgatiśodhani Tāre Tāriṇi Svāhā*. From the *Sūtra of the Twenty-One Homages to the Noble Mother Tārā*.
